entities.name: Pyrrhus II of Epirus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pyrrhus II, a scion of the Aeacid dynasty, reigned as King of Epirus from approximately 255 BCE to 237 BCE, and again briefly before his death in 233 BCE. As the son of Olympias II and Alexander II, he inherited a kingdom grappling with the lingering ambitions of its more famous namesake, Pyrrhus I, and the encroaching power of Macedon and the Aetolian League. His reign marks a critical, yet ultimately tragic, phase in the decline of an independent Epirus, characterized by internal strife and the complex geopolitical maneuvering of the Hellenistic world following the Diadochi wars. His brief periods of rule were punctuated by regencies and power struggles, underscoring the instability that would ultimately lead to the end of the Aeacid monarchy and the rise of the Epirote League.

Initially ascending to the throne as a minor, Pyrrhus II ruled under the regency of his formidable mother, Olympias II, who sought to maintain Epirus's autonomy amidst external pressures. During his active reign, he engaged in military campaigns, most notably against the Aetolian League, to secure his borders and assert Epirus's influence in western Greece. He also formed strategic alliances, including the marriage of his sister Phthia to Demetrius II Aetolicus of Macedon, a move intended to counter the Aetolian threat but which ultimately entangled Epirus further in Macedonian politics. His attempts to consolidate power were often undermined by internal aristocratic factions and the ambitions of his own family members, particularly his brother Ptolemy, who also briefly held regal authority.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Pyrrhus II's reign, though brief, was a crucial transitional period that directly led to the collapse of the Aeacid monarchy and the establishment of the Epirote League, fundamentally altering the political landscape of Epirus for decades to come.
